title: Hom out of an extension by zero from a stratum
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be an admissible commutative condensed coefficient ring, namely a finite commutative ring killed by a power of $\ell$, or $\mathbf Z_\ell$, $\mathcal O_E$, $\mathbf Q_\ell$, $E$, or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, with $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite. Use the pulled-back coefficient sheaves $\Lambda_T$ on the small pro-étale sites, taken in the size convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $i\colon Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion whose complementary open immersion $j\colon X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact (each inverse image of an affine open is quasi-compact), let $u\colon S\hookrightarrow Z$ be open, and put $a=i\circ u$ and $a_!:=i_*u_!$. Define $\underline\Gamma_Z(M)=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$ and let $R\underline\Gamma_Z$ be its unbounded right derived functor, as in [det-lem-formal-closed-support-adjunction]. Let $L$ be a finite locally projective $\Lambda_S$-module, meaning that on a covering of each object of $S_{\mathrm{proét}}$ it is a direct summand of $\Lambda_S^r$ for finite $r$, and put $L^\vee=\mathcal Hom_{\Lambda_S}(L,\Lambda_S)$. All derived categories here are the unbounded categories of modules over these coefficient sheaves, rather than derived-complete or constructible subcategories; $L$ denotes $L[0]$. Write $R\operatorname{Hom}_T(A,B)$ for the global derived Hom complex, computed by global sections of the Hom complex into a K-injective representative of $B$, and $H^q(T,B)=H^q(R\Gamma(T,B))$. Then, naturally in $K\in D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$,
$$
R\operatorname{Hom}_X(a_!L,K)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(u_!L,R\underline\Gamma_ZK)
\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_S(L,u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK)\cong R\Gamma\bigl(S,L^\vee\otimes_{\Lambda_S}u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK\bigr).
$$
The tensor product with $L^\vee$ is computed termwise (and agrees with derived tensor). In particular, for every integer $q$ there is a natural isomorphism
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(a_!L,K[q])\cong H^q(S,L^\vee\otimes u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK).$$

proof.text: By the definition $a_!=i_*u_!$, apply clause (2) of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-adjunction] with $A=u_!L$. This is allowed because $j$ is quasi-compact and $\Lambda$ is a condensed coefficient ring. It gives the first natural isomorphism $R\operatorname{Hom}_X(a_!L,K)\cong R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(u_!L,R\underline\Gamma_ZK)$. No exceptional adjoint for a general proper morphism is being assumed.

source.place: first displayed isomorphism; closed-support adjunction clause (2)

proof.text: Set $N=u^*R\underline\Gamma_ZK$. The functor $u_!$ is exact by [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek], and $u_!\dashv u^*$ by [def-sfb-module-open-lower-shriek-adjunction]; the coefficient pullback $u^*$ is exact by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients]. Choose a K-injective representative $J$ of $R\underline\Gamma_ZK$, using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. By [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], $u^*J$ is K-injective. Termwise adjunction gives an isomorphism of complexes of global morphisms $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_Z(u_!L,J)\cong\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_S(L,u^*J)$: in degree $q$ it is the ordinary adjunction $\operatorname{Hom}_Z(u_!L,J^q)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(L,u^*J^q)$, and naturality in $J^q$ identifies postcomposition by the differential. These are the two global derived Hom complexes, giving the second isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; termwise adjunction as in the blueprint second isomorphism

proof.text: For any $\Lambda_S$-module $M$, define evaluation $e_M:L^\vee\otimes M\to\mathcal Hom(L,M)$ by $\varphi\otimes m\mapsto(l\mapsto\varphi(l)m)$, using [def-pur-sheaf-hom] and [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For $L=\Lambda_S^r$, both sides are $M^r$ and this is the identity in coordinates. On a covering with a splitting $L\oplus L'=\Lambda_S^r$, this isomorphism is block diagonal for the two summands, so its $L$ block is an isomorphism; local inverses agree on overlaps since they invert the same evaluation map, and hence glue. The same splitting shows that $L\otimes-$ and $L^\vee\otimes-$ are locally summands of $(-)^r$ and preserve exact sequences. Indeed kernels are sectionwise and local lifts of sections through an epimorphism can be obtained in all finitely many coordinates on a common refinement, by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Thus they are exact as functors on sheaves. For any acyclic complex $B$, $B\otimes L$ and $B\otimes L^\vee$ are locally direct summands of $B^r$, hence acyclic. This is precisely K-flatness of $L[0]$ and $L^\vee[0]$ in [def-pc-kflat-complex].

source.place: Tag 08JJ, lemma-dual-perfect-complex, finite projective evaluation calculation; Tag 06YN, definition-K-flat

proof.text: For the K-injective complex $I=u^*J$ representing $N$, [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] computes $R\mathcal Hom_S(L,N)$ by $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L[0],I)$. This Hom complex is K-injective by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective], since step 3 proves $L[0]$ K-flat. Consequently $R\Gamma(S,R\mathcal Hom_S(L,N))$ is represented by its ordinary global sections, by [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. By [def-pur-sheaf-hom], these global sections are exactly the complex $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet_S(L[0],I)$ defining $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(L,N)$. Apply the evaluation isomorphisms $e_{I^q}$ of step 3 in each degree. Their naturality with respect to $d_I$ identifies $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L[0],I)$ with $L^\vee\otimes I$. Exactness of tensor with $L^\vee$ makes this complex a representative of $L^\vee\otimes N$; its K-flatness shows that this is also the derived tensor. This proves $R\operatorname{Hom}_S(L,N)\cong R\Gamma(S,L^\vee\otimes N)$, the third isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0A96, lemma-RHom-from-K-flat-into-K-injective; Tag 08J7, section-internal-hom; Tag 08JA, lemma-section-RHom-over-U

proof.text: Each isomorphism above is induced by adjunction or evaluation, so it commutes with maps of K-injective representatives. Such representatives and their maps compute derived morphisms, and changing them gives homotopy-equivalent representatives, by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived]. This proves naturality in $K$. For an integer $q$, a degree-$q$ cocycle in the global Hom complex is a chain map from $a_!L[0]$ to a K-injective representative of $K[q]$; boundaries are precisely null-homotopic maps, as follows by substituting in the differential of [def-pur-hom-complex]. The same K-injective comparison identifies this quotient with $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(X)}(a_!L,K[q])$. Taking degree-$q$ cohomology of the isomorphisms gives the stated $H^q(S,-)$ formula. No boundedness or constructibility assumption is used.
